 "path": "memory/continual_arc_uniform_line_recolor.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC: recolor full-length marker lines

## Observed task pattern (task-fcbeee9f)

A grid uses a background/pattern color and a distinct marker color. One or more complete rows/columns are uniformly the marker color and act as separators/borders. Recolor every cell in each complete uniform marker-color line to the indicated output color; leave all other cells, including isolated marker-colored cells and partial runs, unchanged. Preserve dimensions.

### Evidence
- Demo input was 13x6 with color 7 as the patterned field and color 0 as marker. The entire last column (all 0) and complete rows 8, 9, and 11 (all 0) became color 2 in output. Other 0 cells embedded within patterned rows remained 0.
- Test used colors 8 (pattern field) and 6 (marker). Complete all-6 separators were row 6 and columns 7, 18, and 21. The correct output changed exactly those lines from 6 to 2; all other 6 cells remained unchanged.

## Procedure
1. Inspect the grid for rows/columns that are entirely one candidate marker color (typically a contrasting color); do not infer from a majority or from local segments.
2. Use the demo to identify the replacement color: in this pattern, fully uniform marker lines map to color 2.
3. Copy the grid and change only the cells belonging to those complete uniform rows/columns to 2. Overlaps are simply changed once.
4. Preserve every non-line cell exactly, even if it has the marker color. Check row/column dimensions and output JSON before submitting.

Avoid the tempting but incorrect rule of recoloring every occurrence of the marker color: scattered marker pixels are part of the pattern and must stay unchanged."
